claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has an as-processed hierarchical heterostructure spanning micro- to nanoscales.
The HfNbTiVAl10 heterostructure contains varying grain sizes, phase morphologies, and interface densities.
High-resolution electron microscopy can provide quantitative grain-size, phase-boundary, interface-density, and heterogeneity descriptors for the alloy.
An ML model trained on imaging descriptors and mechanical-test data can predict the tensile and fracture properties of HfNbTiVAl10.
Grain-size distribution, phase interfaces, and local heterogeneity mediate the elastic response of HfNbTiVAl10.
Grain-size distribution, phase interfaces, and local heterogeneity mediate the plastic and yield response of HfNbTiVAl10.
Grain-size distribution, phase interfaces, and local heterogeneity mediate the fracture response of HfNbTiVAl10.
Physics-based information will enable the ML framework to select and weight the microstructural features most relevant to mechanical response.
The resulting surrogate will directly correlate hierarchical microstructural descriptors with elasticity, yielding, and fracture responses.
The physics-informed ML framework will reduce computational complexity relative to established multiscale simulations.
The framework will capture multiscale interactions governing elasticity, yielding, and fracture.
Prediction error for Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior will be reduced by roughly 20–30% relative to conventional simulations.
Predictions will be generated 5–10 times faster than with conventional simulations.
Current state-of-the-art multiscale simulations have high computational cost.
Current simulations have limited accuracy because they incompletely represent the microstructure.
The approach may fail when imaging omits important phase boundaries, defects, or other essential features.
The approach may fail when the heterostructure evolves during loading in ways not represented by static pre-loading descriptors.
Predictive gains depend on imaging quality, training-set representativeness, and training-set size.
